answer_summary.method: ΔE(4.4) = (8.45 − 7.59)·235 = 202.1 MeV per fission (derived answer-blind; the printed 200 MeV fallback was not needed); E = 30000 t × 4.184 GJ/t = 1.2552e14 J; TN = E/ΔE with 1 eV = 1.602176634e-19 J; m(²³⁵U fissioned) = TN·0.23504/N_A kg = 1.513 kg; m(enriched) = m_fissioned/(0.33·0.90) = 5.09 kg.

assumptions: 1 eV = 1.602176634e-19 J exactly (2019 SI definition) — not printed in the problem; trusted general law
Avogadro constant N_A = 6.02214076e23 mol^-1 exactly (2019 SI definition) — not printed in the problem; trusted general law
Standard SI prefixes (1 kt = 1000 t, 1 GJ = 1e9 J, 1 MeV = 1e6 eV) and molar-mass convention (M in g/mol equals isotope mass in a.u.)
Physical model stated implicitly by the problem: each fission releases ΔE; the fissioned ²³⁵U mass is 33% of the total ²³⁵U mass, which is 90% by mass of the enriched uranium
Part 4.4 derived inline from printed binding energies: free-neutron binding neglected, so ΔE = 235·(8.45−7.59) MeV (the absorbed neutron's binding cancels between sides)
source_gaps: The problem statement does not print the MeV↔J conversion factor or Avogadro's constant; the exact SI values were used under the trusted_general_law policy and are disclosed here. All other numeric inputs are printed in the problem (pages Q4-1, Q4-2, Q4-3).
